title: VLAN 30 access port left in default VLAN
symptom: PC1 on Fa0/5 cannot reach the file server in VLAN 30. It gets an IP but no connectivity to anything.
topologyNotes: L2 switch SW1 with VLAN 10 (clients) and VLAN 30 (servers). Fa0/5 should be an access port in VLAN 30.

showOutputs.output:
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/5, Fa0/6, Fa0/7, Fa0/8
10   Clients                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
30   Servers                          active    Fa0/10

Name: Fa0/5
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

expectedFault: Fa0/5 is still assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30.
knownFix: Run "interface Fa0/5" then "switchport access vlan 30" on SW1.

title: Trunk missing allowed VLAN
symptom: Devices in VLAN 20 on SW2 cannot reach VLAN 20 devices on SW1 across the trunk link, but VLAN 10 works fine.
topologyNotes: SW1 and SW2 connected via Gi0/1 trunk. VLANs 10, 20, 30 exist on both switches.

showOutputs.output:
Port      Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1     on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port      Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1     1,10,30

expectedFault: VLAN 20 is not included in the trunk allowed VLAN list.
knownFix: Run "switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20" on the Gi0/1 trunk interface of both switches.

title: DHCP scope exhausted
symptom: New PCs joining VLAN 10 fail to receive an IP address; existing PCs still work.
topologyNotes: Router-on-a-stick providing DHCP for VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/26 - only 64 addresses).

showOutputs.output:
Pool VLAN10_POOL :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Subnet size (first/last)       : 0 / 0
 Total addresses                : 62
 Leased addresses               : 62
 Pending event                  : none

expectedFault: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 has 62 usable addresses, all leased - pool exhaustion.
knownFix: Expand the subnet (e.g. to /24) or reduce the DHCP lease time, then re-run "ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL" with the wider network.

title: DNS server unreachable from client subnet
symptom: PCs can ping 8.8.8.8 by IP but "ping www.cisco.pt" fails with "Ping request could not find host".
topologyNotes: Clients use DHCP-assigned DNS server 10.0.0.53 hosted on a separate VLAN reachable through the core router.

showOutputs.output:
10.0.10.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan10
10.0.0.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan99

expectedFault: DNS server IP is configured, but no route/ACL issue was visible; ICMP to raw IP works so L3 path exists - likely DNS service down or ACL blocking UDP/53 specifically.
knownFix: Verify the DNS server process is running and reachable on UDP/53 (not just ICMP); check any ACL for a udp eq 53 permit statement.

title: Missing default route on edge router
symptom: Internal LAN devices can reach each other and internal servers, but nothing outside the local network (e.g. no Internet access).
topologyNotes: Edge router R1 connects internal LAN to ISP via Se0/0/0. Internal routing between VLANs works fine.

showOutputs.output:
C    192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C    192.168.2.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
C    203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0

expectedFault: No default route (0.0.0.0/0) exists pointing to the ISP - no gateway of last resort configured.
knownFix: Configure "ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1" (or the correct next hop) on R1.

title: Static route pointing to wrong next hop
symptom: Branch office (192.168.30.0/24) cannot reach HQ subnet (192.168.10.0/24); traceroute stops after the branch router.
topologyNotes: Branch router R2 has a static route to HQ. WAN link between R2 and R1 is 172.16.0.0/30.

showOutputs.output:
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 172.16.0.5/30

expectedFault: Static route next hop 172.16.0.6 is outside the /30 WAN subnet (172.16.0.4-172.16.0.7 usable is only .5 and .6, but .6 should be the R1 side - verify actual R1 IP; if R1 is .5 itself this is a self-referential/wrong next hop).
knownFix: Correct the static route next-hop IP to match R1's actual Serial0/0/0 address, e.g. "ip route 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 172.16.0.6" only if .6 is truly R1; otherwise fix to the correct neighbor IP.

title: ACL blocking Telnet management access
symptom: Network admin cannot Telnet into R1 (192.168.1.1) from the management VLAN, connection times out.
topologyNotes: R1 has VTY lines protected by an access-class ACL restricting management access.

showOutputs.output:
Standard IP access list MGMT_ACL
    10 permit 192.168.99.10
    20 deny any (5 matches)

line vty 0 4
 access-class MGMT_ACL in
 login local

expectedFault: MGMT_ACL only permits a single host (192.168.99.10); the admin's actual source IP is being denied by the implicit/explicit deny.
knownFix: Add a permit line for the admin's subnet/host in MGMT_ACL, e.g. "permit 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255".

title: NAT overload missing outside interface
symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the Internet despite having correct default routes; "show ip nat translations" is empty.
topologyNotes: R1 performs PAT (NAT overload) from inside VLAN 10 to the ISP-facing interface.

showOutputs.output:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip nat inside
ip nat inside source list NAT_ACL interface Serial0/0/0 overload
Total translations: 0 (0 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)

expectedFault: Serial0/0/0 (the outside/ISP-facing interface) is missing "ip nat outside", so NAT never triggers.
knownFix: Apply "ip nat outside" under "interface Serial0/0/0".

title: NAT ACL too narrow, excludes new subnet
symptom: PCs in newly added VLAN 40 (192.168.40.0/24) cannot access the Internet; VLAN 10 and 20 work fine.
topologyNotes: PAT configured with NAT_ACL matching only the original two subnets.

showOutputs.output:
Standard IP access list NAT_ACL
    10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
    20 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255

expectedFault: NAT_ACL does not include 192.168.40.0/24, so traffic from VLAN 40 is never translated.
knownFix: Add "permit 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255" to NAT_ACL.

title: Switchport mode mismatch breaks trunk
symptom: Inter-switch link between SW1 and SW2 carries only VLAN 1 traffic; other VLANs across the link fail entirely.
topologyNotes: Gi0/1 on SW1 and SW2 should form an 802.1q trunk.

showOutputs.output:
Port      Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1     on           802.1q         trunking      1

Name: Gi0/1
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access

expectedFault: SW2 Gi0/1 is configured as a static access port, not trunk, causing a mode mismatch with SW1.
knownFix: On SW2 Gi0/1, run "switchport mode trunk" and "switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q" if required.

title: Native VLAN mismatch causing CDP warnings
symptom: Intermittent connectivity issues and CDP native VLAN mismatch messages appear in the switch log between SW1 and SW3.
topologyNotes: Trunk link Gi0/2 connects SW1 and SW3.

showOutputs.output:
Port      Mode   Encapsulation  Status     Native vlan
Gi0/2     on     802.1q         trunking   1

Port      Mode   Encapsulation  Status     Native vlan
Gi0/2     on     802.1q         trunking   99

expectedFault: Native VLAN differs between the two ends of the trunk (VLAN 1 vs VLAN 99).
knownFix: Set matching native VLANs on both ends, e.g. "switchport trunk native vlan 99" on SW1 Gi0/2.

title: Duplicate IP address on client subnet
symptom: Two PCs on VLAN 10 have intermittent connectivity; both occasionally lose network access when the other is active.
topologyNotes: Static IPs assigned manually to lab PCs; DHCP not used on this VLAN by design.

showOutputs.output:
Internet  10.0.10.15   -   0060.2F3A.1B2C  ARPA  Vlan10
Internet  10.0.10.15   -   0060.2F9C.44D1  ARPA  Vlan10

expectedFault: Two different MAC addresses map to the same IP 10.0.10.15 - duplicate static IP assignment.
knownFix: Reassign a unique IP to one of the two PCs and clear the ARP cache/table on the switch and router.

title: Wrong subnet mask on client causes gateway unreachable
symptom: PC on VLAN 10 cannot ping its own default gateway despite correct-looking IP and gateway values.
expectedFault: Subnet mask 255.255.255.192 (/26) puts the gateway 192.168.10.1 in a different subnet block than host .55 - verify subnet boundaries.
knownFix: Correct the subnet mask on the PC to 255.255.255.0 to match the SVI configuration.

title: Gateway IP mismatch after SVI renumbering
symptom: All PCs in VLAN 20 lost Internet and inter-VLAN access after a network re-addressing change.
topologyNotes: VLAN 20 SVI was renumbered from 192.168.20.1/24 to 192.168.21.1/24; PCs use static gateways.

showOutputs.output:
interface Vlan20
 ip address 192.168.21.1 255.255.255.0

expectedFault: PC still references the old gateway 192.168.20.1, but the SVI is now 192.168.21.1 on a different subnet.
knownFix: Update PC static IP/gateway to the new 192.168.21.0/24 scheme, or revert the SVI change.

title: Wireless client cannot authenticate to WPA2 SSID
symptom: Laptop repeatedly prompts for the Wi-Fi password and never connects to "LAB-WIFI".
topologyNotes: Wireless router configured with WPA2-PSK on SSID LAB-WIFI.

showOutputs.output:
ssid LAB-WIFI
 authentication open
 wpa-psk ascii 0 CorrectHorseBattery

expectedFault: Authentication is set to "open" while a WPA-PSK key is also configured - conflicting security mode causes client handshake failures.
knownFix: Set authentication mode to WPA2-PSK consistently (not "open") so the pre-shared key is actually enforced.

title: Wireless SSID broadcast disabled confuses users
symptom: Users report they cannot find "LAB-WIFI" in their available networks list, though wired clients see the AP is up.
topologyNotes: SSID broadcast toggled off during a prior lab.

showOutputs.output:
ssid LAB-WIFI
 broadcast-ssid disable

expectedFault: SSID broadcast is disabled, hiding the network from client scan lists.
knownFix: Re-enable SSID broadcast or have users manually enter the hidden SSID.

title: Interface administratively shut down
symptom: Branch office is completely unreachable from HQ; link light on the WAN interface at the branch appears off.
topologyNotes: R2 Serial0/0/1 connects branch to HQ via a leased line.

showOutputs.output: Serial0/0/1            172.16.1.2      YES manual administratively down down

expectedFault: Serial0/0/1 is administratively down - someone issued a "shutdown" command.
knownFix: Enter "interface Serial0/0/1" then "no shutdown".

title: Duplex mismatch causing slow/erratic performance
symptom: File transfers to the server on Fa0/10 are extremely slow and the switch log shows many CRC/late-collision errors.
topologyNotes: Server NIC manually set to full-duplex; switch port set to auto.

showOutputs.output:
Fa0/10 is up, line protocol is up
  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s
  1532 input errors, 985 CRC, 640 late collisions

expectedFault: High late-collision/CRC counts alongside full-duplex on the switch side suggest a duplex mismatch with the server NIC (half vs full).
knownFix: Set both the switch port and server NIC to the same duplex/speed (auto/auto, or match full/100 explicitly).

title: Router-on-a-stick missing subinterface for new VLAN
symptom: Newly created VLAN 50 devices cannot reach any other VLAN, though VLAN 50 itself works for local L2 traffic.
topologyNotes: Router-on-a-stick R1 with Gi0/0 trunked to SW1, subinterfaces for VLAN 10/20/30 exist.

showOutputs.output:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 encapsulation dot1Q 10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30

expectedFault: No Gi0/0.50 subinterface exists for VLAN 50, so the router cannot route for that VLAN.
knownFix: Create "interface GigabitEthernet0/0.50", set "encapsulation dot1Q 50", and assign the appropriate IP address.

title: OSPF neighbor stuck in EXSTART due to MTU mismatch
symptom: R1 and R2 form an OSPF adjacency that never progresses past EXSTART; routes are not being learned.
topologyNotes: R1 and R2 run OSPF area 0 over a point-to-point link; R2 interface has a non-default MTU.

showOutputs.output:
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
2.2.2.2           1   EXSTART/  -      00:00:35    172.16.0.2      Serial0/0/0
MTU 1500 bytes
MTU 1400 bytes

expectedFault: MTU mismatch (1500 on R1 vs 1400 on R2) prevents OSPF database exchange from completing, stalling adjacency in EXSTART.
knownFix: Set matching MTU on both interfaces ("ip mtu 1500" on R2 Serial0/0/0) and clear the OSPF process.

title: Access list applied in wrong direction
symptom: Internal users can no longer reach the web server even though the ACL was meant to only restrict inbound Internet traffic.
topologyNotes: ACL 101 applied on Gi0/0 (LAN-facing) instead of Se0/0/0 (WAN-facing).

showOutputs.output:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip access-group 101 in

Extended IP access list 101
    10 deny tcp any any eq 80
    20 permit ip any any

expectedFault: ACL 101 is applied inbound on the LAN interface Gi0/0, blocking internal users' outbound HTTP requests instead.
knownFix: Remove "ip access-group 101 in" from Gi0/0 and apply it correctly on the WAN-facing interface.

title: Standard ACL used where extended ACL was needed
symptom: Attempt to block only Telnet (TCP/23) to R2 from a specific subnet instead blocks all traffic from that subnet.
topologyNotes: Standard ACL matches source address only and cannot filter by port/protocol.

showOutputs.output:
Standard IP access list 10
    10 deny 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255
    20 permit any

expectedFault: A standard ACL matches source address only and cannot filter by port/protocol, so it denies ALL traffic from 192.168.50.0/24.
knownFix: Replace with an extended ACL, e.g. "access-list 110 deny tcp 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 23" followed by permit any any.

title: Port security violation shutting down access port
symptom: PC on Fa0/8 suddenly lost network connectivity after an unauthorized laptop was plugged in.
topologyNotes: Fa0/8 has port security with maximum 1 MAC, violation mode shutdown.

showOutputs.output:
Port Security: Enabled
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
Violation Mode: Shutdown
Maximum MAC Addresses: 1
SecurityViolation Count: 1

expectedFault: Port security detected a second MAC address on Fa0/8 and placed it into err-disabled state.
knownFix: Remove unauthorized device, run "shutdown" and "no shutdown" on Fa0/8 to clear err-disabled state.

title: Spanning-tree blocking the only active uplink
symptom: SW3 has two uplinks but one is blocked by STP. Traffic fails when the active link's transceiver is bad.
topologyNotes: SW3 uplinks Gi0/1 and Gi0/2 to two core switches; STP root port is down but alternate hasn't transitioned.

showOutputs.output:
Interface           Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type
Gi0/1               Root FWD 4         128.1    P2p
Gi0/2               Altn BLK 4         128.2    P2p
GigabitEthernet0/1 is down, line protocol is down (notconnect)

expectedFault: STP root port Gi0/1 is physically down, and alternate Gi0/2 has not transitioned to forwarding.
knownFix: Verify Gi0/1 physical connection; confirm Gi0/2 transitions to forwarding after STP recalculates.

title: Inter-VLAN routing ACL blocks server access (reference case)
symptom: PC gets IP but cannot reach server in VLAN 30; gateway ping works.
topologyNotes: L3 switch with VLAN 10 (clients) and VLAN 30 (servers), SVIs configured for inter-VLAN routing.

showOutputs.output:
10.0.10.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan10
10.0.30.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan30

Extended IP access list BLOCK_SERVERS
    10 deny ip 10.0.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.0.30.0 0.0.0.255
    20 permit ip any any

expectedFault: ACL BLOCK_SERVERS explicitly denies client-to-server traffic before the permit any any.
knownFix: Add a permit entry above the deny for the required traffic, or remove/adjust the deny line.

title: DHCP relay (helper-address) missing on remote VLAN
symptom: PCs on VLAN 40 never receive an IP lease; VLAN 10 (with DHCP server) works fine.
topologyNotes: Central DHCP server lives on VLAN 10; VLAN 40 is routed separately.

showOutputs.output:
interface Vlan40
 ip address 192.168.40.1 255.255.255.0
! no ip helper-address configured

expectedFault: No "ip helper-address" is configured on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the server.
knownFix: Add "ip helper-address <DHCP-server-IP>" under "interface Vlan40".

title: Excluded address range too broad on DHCP pool
symptom: Only the first two PCs in VLAN 10 receive IP addresses via DHCP; others fail.
topologyNotes: DHCP pool for 192.168.10.0/24 configured with excluded-address range.

showOutputs.output:
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.253
ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.10.1

expectedFault: The excluded range (192.168.10.1 - 192.168.10.253) removes nearly the entire pool, leaving only .254.
knownFix: Narrow the excluded range to just the statically assigned addresses (e.g. .1 to .10).

title: DNS forwarder pointing to unreachable upstream
symptom: Internal DNS resolves local hosts but external lookups (e.g. google.com) time out.
topologyNotes: Internal DNS server configured to forward unresolved queries to public DNS.

showOutputs.output: Request timed out. Success rate is 0 percent (0/4)

expectedFault: The configured upstream DNS forwarder 198.51.100.99 is unreachable.
knownFix: Correct the forwarder IP to a reachable upstream DNS server.

title: HSRP misconfiguration - no active gateway
symptom: PCs using virtual gateway IP intermittently lose gateway connectivity.
topologyNotes: R1 and R2 run HSRP for VLAN 10 with virtual IP 192.168.10.1.

showOutputs.output:
Interface  Grp  Pri P State    Active       Standby      Virtual IP
Vl10       10   100   Standby  unknown      local        192.168.10.1

Interface  Grp  Pri P State    Active       Standby      Virtual IP
Vl10       10   100   Standby  unknown      local        192.168.10.1

expectedFault: Both HSRP routers report themselves as Standby with Active unknown - multicast hellos are blocked.
knownFix: Verify VLAN 10 connectivity/trunking between R1 and R2; verify multicast/UDP 1985 is not blocked.

title: Wireless client wrong security type selected
symptom: One specific laptop cannot join SSID while all other devices connect successfully.
topologyNotes: AP requires WPA2-PSK (AES) but laptop profile was created with WPA-TKIP.

showOutputs.output:
SSID: LAB-WIFI
Security: WPA-PSK (TKIP)
AP requires: WPA2-PSK (AES)

expectedFault: The laptop's profile uses outdated WPA-TKIP while the AP only accepts WPA2-PSK/AES.
knownFix: Delete the saved Wi-Fi profile on the laptop and reconnect to negotiate WPA2-PSK/AES correctly.

title: Access port configured as trunk by mistake
symptom: A single lab PC shows untagged VLAN warnings and cannot get a DHCP lease.
topologyNotes: Fa0/12 should be a simple access port in VLAN 10.

showOutputs.output:
Name: Fa0/12
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

expectedFault: Fa0/12 was configured as a trunk port instead of access.
knownFix: Run "switchport mode access" and "switchport access vlan 10" on Fa0/12.

title: Extended ACL missing "established" for return traffic
symptom: Internal users can initiate sessions but return traffic is dropped; sessions hang.
topologyNotes: Inbound ACL on WAN interface intended to allow return traffic for internal sessions.

showOutputs.output:
Extended IP access list 120
    10 permit tcp any any eq 80
    20 deny ip any any

expectedFault: The inbound WAN ACL lacks the "established" keyword, blocking incoming TCP response packets.
knownFix: Add "permit tcp any any established" to allow return traffic.
